nodes.label: Hermes Plugin Manifest (superpowers v6.4.2, author obra, provides pre_llm_call hook)
Installing Superpowers for OpenCode (.opencode/INSTALL.md)
OpenCode V1 plugin config (`plugin` key, git-backed package spec)
OpenCode V2 plugin config (`plugins` key, requires OpenCode 2.0.4+)
nodes.rationale: OpenCode 2.0.4 and 2.0.7 reject a configured direct JavaScript-file path, so a local V2 install points at the repository directory containing index.js; discovered plugin symlinks remain supported.

nodes.label: Migration from the old symlink-based OpenCode install
Pinning Superpowers version via git tag in the plugin spec (#v6.4.2; V2 needs v6.4.1+)
nodes.rationale: Some OpenCode and Bun versions pin the resolved git dependency in a lockfile or cache, so a restart may not pick up the newest commit; v6.3.0 and earlier only load on V1.

nodes.label: Windows workaround: npm install --prefix and absolute local package path in opencode.json
nodes.rationale: Some Windows OpenCode builds mishandle git+https cache paths and Bun cannot find git.exe; OpenCode does not expand ~, so a ~/... entry is treated as a package name.

nodes.label: Superpowers for OpenCode README
OpenCode skills directory registration (V1 config hook -> config.skills.paths; V2 setup() -> ctx.skill.transform())
nodes.rationale: Registering the skills directory through host-flavor-specific APIs lets OpenCode discover all superpowers skills without symlinks or manual config.

nodes.label: OpenCode bootstrap injection (V1 experimental.chat.messages.transform; V2 ctx.session.hook("context"); controller-only, compaction-aware)
nodes.rationale: Only controller sessions receive the using-superpowers bootstrap as transient model context; delegated child sessions keep native skills but not the bootstrap. After V2 compaction the bootstrap goes into the first retained user message or a transient message after the checkpoint, leaving saved history unchanged. Failed session lookups keep the bootstrap and are not cached.

nodes.label: OpenCode V1/V2 tool mapping (task->subagent, apply_patch->patch, bash->shell, todo dropped in V2)
nodes.rationale: Skills speak in actions rather than naming any one runtime's tools, so the bootstrap maps them to the tools each OpenCode flavor actually exposes; V2 renamed task to subagent, apply_patch to patch, bash to shell, and dropped the todo tool entirely.

nodes.label: OpenCode skill priority (V2: project > personal > superpowers; V1 1.18.31: bundled superpowers wins)
nodes.rationale: On tested V1 1.18.31 bundled Superpowers skills take precedence over same-named personal/project skills, so distinct names are recommended.

nodes.label: using-git-worktrees Skill (isolated workspace via native tools or git worktree fallback)
Core principle: detect existing isolation, then native tools, then git; never fight the harness
Step 0: Detect existing isolation (GIT_DIR vs GIT_COMMON)
nodes.rationale: Harness-created isolation and submodules both fool eyeballing; the detection commands settle it.

nodes.label: Submodule guard (git rev-parse --show-superproject-working-tree)
nodes.rationale: GIT_DIR != GIT_COMMON is also true inside git submodules, so a submodule must be treated as a normal repo, not a worktree.

nodes.label: Consent before creating a worktree (honor declared preference)
Step 1a: Native worktree tools preferred (e.g. EnterWorktree, /worktree)
nodes.rationale: Native tools own directory placement, branch creation and cleanup; running git worktree add when a native tool exists creates phantom state the harness cannot see or manage (the #1 mistake).

nodes.label: Step 1b: Git worktree fallback (git worktree add)
Worktree directory selection (instructions > .worktrees/ > worktrees/ > default .worktrees/)
nodes.rationale: Explicit user preference always beats observed filesystem state.

nodes.label: Safety verification: git check-ignore before creating a project-local worktree
nodes.rationale: Prevents accidentally committing worktree contents to the repository.

nodes.label: Sandbox fallback: work in place when git worktree add is denied
Step 2: Project setup auto-detection (npm, cargo, pip/poetry, go)
Step 3: Verify clean test baseline
nodes.rationale: A dirty baseline makes every later failure ambiguous; proceeding past failures is the human partner's call.

nodes.label: Common Rationalizations (Excuse/Reality table) for worktrees
writing-plans Skill (implementation plans from a spec, before touching code)
Plan reader: capable engineer without codebase/spec context; document decisions, not code
nodes.rationale: They write idiomatic code once they know the exact interface and test and make reasonable choices where the plan leaves one open; what they cannot know is what you decided: files, names, signatures, spec values, and which tests prove each task.

nodes.label: Plan save path docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md
Scope Check (one plan per independent subsystem)
nodes.rationale: Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

nodes.label: File Structure mapping before defining tasks
nodes.rationale: This is where decomposition decisions get locked in; focused files are easier to hold in context and edits to them are more reliable.

nodes.label: Task Right-Sizing (smallest unit with its own test cycle and reviewer gate)
nodes.rationale: Fold setup, config, scaffolding and docs into the task that needs them; split only where a reviewer could meaningfully reject one task while approving its neighbor.

nodes.label: Step granularity: one action with a checkable result
Plan Document Header (Goal, Architecture, Tech Stack, Spec pointer, required execution sub-skill)
nodes.rationale: The plan argues from the spec, so the spec travels with it and executors read both.

nodes.label: Global Constraints section (project-wide spec requirements copied verbatim)
nodes.rationale: Every task's requirements implicitly include this section, so exact values reach implementers and reviewers.

nodes.label: Review Focus section (five spec-implied input classes/failure modes no task test exercises)
nodes.rationale: The spec is a vision document: its silence on an input is not permission for that input to break the program; each line gets a pinning test in the owning task.

nodes.label: Task Structure template (Files, Interfaces, checkbox TDD steps, commit)
Per-task Interfaces block (Consumes/Produces exact signatures)
nodes.rationale: A task's implementer sees only their own task; this block is how they learn the names and types neighboring tasks use.

nodes.label: What a Step Contains: unambiguous, not complete
nodes.rationale: A plan is the set of decisions the implementer cannot make alone. A plan longer than the code it describes has written the code instead; lines that decide nothing (TBD, "handle edge cases") are the opposite failure. Test steps carry names and assertions, code steps carry exact signatures and spec values, bodies only for undetermined algorithms or fixed copy.

nodes.label: Self-Review checklist (spec coverage, step scan, type consistency, Review Focus, proportion)
nodes.rationale: Run inline by the plan author, not as a subagent dispatch; fix issues in place.

nodes.label: Proportion check: plan length vs spec length
nodes.rationale: A plan several times longer than its spec is a transcript of the program; when code blocks dominate, replace bodies with signatures, test names and assertions.

nodes.label: Execution Handoff (user reviews saved plan; Subagent-driven vs Native, recommend one)
nodes.rationale: Approving an idea or scope is not approving a plan the user has not seen; an explicitly supplied execution method is preserved, otherwise one is recommended with a reason drawn from the plan.

nodes.label: Superpowers Release Notes
Superpowers Project
v6.4.2 (2026-09-25): leaner plans from writing-plans
nodes.rationale: Some frontier models (including Opus 5.5) got overzealous during plan writing and sometimes implemented the whole project while designing the plan; the new skill keeps planning focused. Reproducing the report, scratch builds went away and plans took ~1/4 the time and ~1/3 the tokens, while still executing 9/9 against planted-defect probes on Sonnet 5. Reported by Harper Reed (#2333).

nodes.label: v6.4.1 (2026-09-18): diagnosing-superpowers, Native execution, OpenCode 2.0 / Muse / Qwen Code support
nodes.rationale: v6.4.0 was never shipped; the proving-it-works-with-a-movie skill was held back for robustness work.

nodes.label: v6.3.0 (2026-08-12): Devin CLI and Hermes Agent support, brainstorming ceremony scaling, SDD conflict rulings, Spec: pointer in plans
v6.2.0 (2026-07-23): plan-scoped SDD workspace, review-fix loop resume, compression campaign, Git Bash SessionStart
v6.0.0 (2026-06-16): one reviewer per task, plan Global Constraints/Interfaces, visual companion security, vendor-neutral skills, Kimi/Pi/Antigravity
nodes.rationale: In evals Claude Code and Codex produced similar high-quality results roughly twice as fast with almost 50% fewer tokens.

nodes.label: v5.1.0 (2026-04-30): worktree skills rewrite, code-reviewer agent removed, legacy slash commands removed
v5.0.6 (2026-03-24): inline self-review replaces subagent review loops
nodes.rationale: The subagent review loop added ~25 min per run without measurably improving plan quality (5 versions x 5 trials); inline self-review catches 3-5 real bugs in ~30s.

nodes.label: v5.0.0 (2026-03-09): specs/plans directory restructure, visual brainstorming companion, document review system, SDD mandatory on capable harnesses
v4.0.0 (2025-12-17): two-stage SDD code review, DOT flowcharts as executable specs, skill consolidation
v2.0.0: skills repository separation (obra/superpowers-skills)
nodes.rationale: Turned the monolithic plugin into a lightweight shim managing a local clone so skills auto-update, version independently and accept community PRs via git workflows.

nodes.label: No Placeholders section (writing-plans; added v5.0.6, replaced by "What a Step Contains" in v6.4.2)
AGENTS.md as canonical contributor guidelines (CLAUDE.md removed in v6.4.2)
nodes.rationale: Claude Code reads AGENTS.md directly only when no CLAUDE.md exists, so the one-line CLAUDE.md pointer would have hidden the real guidelines; the earlier AGENTS.md->CLAUDE.md symlink was rejected by Muse's installer.

nodes.label: Native (inline) execution mode for executing-plans (#2318)
nodes.rationale: executing-plans was a 64-line stub that measured the same as no plugin; it was rebuilt under SDD's workspace, ledger and stopping rules with one fresh whole-branch review on the most capable model, making it the cheapest way to run a plan.

nodes.label: Reviewers judge spec-silent behavior by reasonable-user expectation, with a "Declined to judge" list (#2319)
nodes.rationale: So a crash on an input the spec never named no longer slides through as Minor.

nodes.label: TDD: the project's suite defines green, not just the task's test file (#2110)
nodes.rationale: Sessions ran only the named test file in 11 of 12 probe runs, so broken neighboring tests went unseen.

nodes.label: Plan-scoped SDD workspace (.superpowers/sdd/<plan-basename>/; same-basename collision fix in v6.4.1)
nodes.rationale: A follow-up plan in the same tree could read the previous plan's ledger as its own progress; plan-scoping makes the answer structural. v6.4.1 fixed same-basename plans sharing a directory where task-brief overwrote the other plan's brief.

nodes.label: Bundled scripts invoked through their interpreter (bash scripts/foo.sh, node render-graphs.js)
nodes.rationale: Packagers (Codex marketplace, MiniMax Code) stripped executable bits, so every documented command failed with Permission denied (#2301, #2134, #2040).

nodes.label: OpenCode 2.0.4+ support (V2 native skill API; bootstrap survives continuation, restart, forks, compaction; child sessions excluded) (#2106, #2306)
SDD review-fix loop resumes the implementer; scoped re-review; five-round circuit breaker
Branch-wide skill compression campaign (recap/persuasion prose removed, arguments folded into rationalization tables)
nodes.rationale: Prose aimed at a reader who already invoked the skill was dead weight; each cut was micro-tested with subagent probes, and the one cut that measurably degraded behavior (TDD "Why Order Matters", 8/10 -> 5/10) was reworked into rationalization rows.

nodes.label: Windows SessionStart hook fixes (run-hook.cmd polyglot wrapper, quoting fixes, Git Bash dispatch via shell: bash)
nodes.rationale: PowerShell parsed the quoted command as an expression and cmd.exe quote-stripping truncated paths with metacharacters, so the bootstrap silently never loaded.

nodes.label: Brainstorming visual companion per-session key security model (closes #1014)
nodes.rationale: The companion server had no authentication: anyone reaching the port could read the brainstorm or inject events treated as user input, including the DNS-rebinding case an origin allowlist cannot catch.

nodes.label: One set of skills, every harness: action-based vocabulary plus per-harness tool references
Two-stage SDD code review (spec compliance then code quality); collapsed into one reviewer in v6.0.0
nodes.rationale: Catches code that is well written but does not match what was requested.

nodes.label: Worktree skills rewrite: environment detection, consent, native tool preference, provenance-based cleanup (PR #1121)
superpowers:code-reviewer named agent removed; merged into code-reviewer.md dispatch template (PR #1299)
nodes.rationale: Single source of truth: the persona/checklist lived in both the agent and the skill template and drifted independently.

nodes.label: OpenCode bootstrap content cached at module level (getBootstrapContent, #1202)
nodes.rationale: The experimental.chat.messages.transform hook fires on every agent step, so re-reading and re-parsing the bootstrap file each step was wasteful.

nodes.label: Document review system (spec/plan reviewer subagent loops; added v5.0.0, replaced by inline self-review in v5.0.6)
Instruction priority hierarchy (user instructions > Superpowers skills > default system prompt)
The Description Trap: skill descriptions must be trigger-only
nodes.rationale: Descriptions containing workflow summaries override the flowchart; the model follows the short description instead of reading the detailed process.

Plan-to-execution pipeline (worktree isolation -> writing-plans -> Subagent-driven or Native execution)
